
{{alias}}( ndims )
    Returns a kernel for applying a one-dimensional strided array reduction
    function to an input ndarray and assigning results to an output ndarray
    having getter and setter accessors.

    The returned function has the following parameters:

    - fcn: wrapper for a one-dimensional strided array reduction function.
    - arrays: array containing one input ndarray descriptor and one output
    ndarray descriptor, followed by any additional ndarray arguments.
    - views: initialized ndarray descriptors representing subarray views.
    - strides: loop dimension strides for the input ndarray.
    - strategy: input ndarray reshape strategy.
    - options: function options which are passed through to `fcn`.

    If `ndims` is greater than the maximum supported number of loop dimensions,
    the function returns `null`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ndims: integer
        Number of loop dimensions.

    Returns
    -------
    fcn: Function|null
        Kernel function.

    Examples
    --------
    > var f = {{alias}}( 2 )
    <Function>


{{alias}}.kernel0d( fcn, arr, views, sx, strategy, opts )
    Performs a reduction over a list of specified dimensions in an input ndarray
    and assigns results to a provided output ndarray.

    The `views` and `sx` parameters are unused. Providing empty arrays for these
    parameters is recommended in order to ensure a monomorphic API.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fcn: Function
        Wrapper for a one-dimensional strided array reduction function.

    arr: Array<Object>
        Array containing one input ndarray descriptor and one output ndarray
        descriptor, followed by any additional ndarray arguments.

    views: Array<Object>
        Initialized ndarray descriptors representing subarray views.

    sx: Array<integer>
        Loop dimension strides for the input ndarray. Should have zero elements.

    strategy: Function
        Input ndarray reshape strategy.

    opts: Object
        Function options which are passed through to `fcn`.


{{alias}}.kernel1d( fcn, arr, views, sx, strategy, opts )

    output ndarray.
